summary: Cowlitz County summit: state tower 1932, wind fall 1950, DNR 40-ft tower 1951, abandoned by 1968; footings reported on company timber land.

facts.design: 40-foot wooden tower with a 14-foot-square DNR cab (1951)
facts.status_note: The summit tower fell in 1950; the 1951 tower was later removed, and foundations are described at the site
facts.agency: Washington Division of Forestry, later Department of Natural Resources

access.note: Company timber land; the company sets access rules. Willhite says non-motorized access was allowed as of 2018, and the company prohibits access during fire danger in dry, hot summers. Willhite's photo captions show a gate on the route.

visit.trail_note: About 7 miles each way on foot or bike, with about 2,000 ft of gain (Willhite). A mountain bike trail network covers much of the mountain.

events.note: Ground-level lookout cabin set up by Long-Bell Lumber Company in cooperation with the Division of Forestry
First tower on the summit, built by the state Division of Forestry. Height is 83 ft in firelookout.com and 92 ft in Willhite.
July 1938 fire with flames on three sides of the mountain; a chief warden telephoned from the tower. Willhite quotes a newspaper saying 300 firefighters were endangered.
Timber tower with a 14 x 14 ft cab built by CCC company 937. Heights differ across sources: 40, 83 and 85 ft.
Cliff Helm listed as the lookout from 1942 to 1952
Summit tower blown over by high winds in October 1950
40-foot tower with a 14-foot DNR cab built by the Washington Department of Natural Resources
Leland Peterson of Bellevue listed as the lookout
Willhite's newspaper item says the tower had not been manned since 1966. Firelookout.com lists Mrs. George Baxter in 1965.
FFLOS says deactivated in 1968, and Willhite says abandoned 1968. Firelookout.com says abandoned 1966.
Firelookout.com says destroyed 1969. Willhite says gone by 1973.

corrections.why: No source gives 100 ft for this site. The 1951 tower, the last one, is 40 ft in FFLOS, firelookout.com and Willhite.

corrections.proposed: Washington Division of Forestry, later Department of Natural Resources
corrections.why: FFLOS names Campbell Group Tree Farm as the current administrator. The state built and ran the lookout, as firelookout.com and Willhite both show.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1932 tower is 83 ft in firelookout.com and 92 ft in Willhite. The 1940 tower is 40, 83 or 85 ft across the sources. Only the 1951 tower's 40 ft is agreed on, so that is the height recorded.
Firelookout.com and a newspaper item reprinted by Willhite give 1966. FFLOS and Willhite's summary give 1968. The story gives both.
Firelookout.com gives destroyed in 1969. Willhite says gone by 1973.
FFLOS names Campbell Group Tree Farm and Willhite names Sierra Pacific as the company allowing access. The story says a timber company manages the land and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Sources agree on the 1932 state tower, the October 1950 wind fall, and the 1951 DNR tower (40 ft, 14-ft cab). They disagree on the 1932 and 1940 heights, the abandonment year (1966 or 1968), the removal year (1969 or 1973) and the landowner. Brief height_m 30.5 (100 ft) has no source; 12.2 m is proposed. Brief agency is the current landowner per FFLOS; this is a judgement call. Willhite's photo captions are undated, so footings are reported as described, not as seen on a visit date. Elevation differs (2,559 ft in FFLOS, 2,577 ft elsewhere); elevation is not in facts. No new photos, since fetched text has no image URLs. Read budget overran: 7 page reads including one repeat of the FFLOS page, plus one search. The Willhite page's 1964 newspaper item has an internal date problem (it says 1964 and also 'not manned since 1966').
